title: Two known noise conditions recovered a fixed drift in six fly and mouse model tests with separate covariance eigenvalues
abstract: We tested whether two stationary covariance matrices identify directed circuit weights when known input noise changes and drift stays fixed. A matrix proof gives unique unrestricted drift if the generalized covariance eigenvalues are all distinct. Three distributed noise designs on each of two published structural graphs, with 75 fly regions and 304 Allen-based mouse parcels, met this numerical test. Exact simulated covariances gave relative drift errors below 1.7e-12. A uniform noise scale adds no information. A single-node change gave many eigenvalue gaps below numerical resolution. At a whitened covariance error bound of 0.001, a direct inverse gave median drift errors of 13.5% in fly and 23.3% in mouse. These are model tests, not fits to measured neural activity. Known noise, fixed drift, complete observation, and linear stationary dynamics are required. Code, proof, scalar results, a figure, and external-input retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Distributed known noise gave separate covariance eigenvalues in six model cases. The direct inverse amplified small synthetic covariance errors. Points show three designs per graph; curves and bands show medians and ranges of nine runs per error size.

citations.reason: Verified external graph matrices and model gain; extends its one-condition ambiguity audit to known two-condition noise.
